operations.evidence: The January 2026 road safety strategy set targets to reduce reported-road KSI casualties by 65% by 2035 and child KSIs by 70% by 2030 against a 2022 to 2024 baseline.
Targets are policy objectives, not observed parcel outcomes.
Injury figures are adjusted to account for changes in police reporting of injury severity.
Adjustments improve comparability but may be more revisable for recently transitioned forces.
The statistics include police-reported public-highway collisions involving at least one motor vehicle, horse rider or pedal cyclist and at least one injured person.
There is no obligation to report every personal-injury collision to police.
The adjusted estimate for seriously injured casualties was 28,355 in 2025, 4% higher than 2024 and 7% lower than 2015.
Adjusted national totals must not be converted directly into local risk scores.
The adjusted estimate for slightly injured casualties was 97,959 in 2025, 1% lower than 2024 and 36% lower than 2015.
Slight injuries are particularly affected by under-reporting.
The estimated fatality rate was 4.5 per billion vehicle miles in 2025, 5% lower than 2024.
A national traffic-exposure rate is not a parcel probability.
The estimated KSI rate was 86.4 per billion vehicle miles in 2025, 2% higher than 2024.
The rate depends on national traffic exposure and severity adjustment.
The estimated all-casualty rate was 369.3 per billion vehicle miles in 2025, 2% lower than 2024.
The rate does not describe any individual road segment or property.
There were an estimated 1,484 casualties in collisions involving e-scooters in 2025, compared with 1,390 in 2024.
E-scooter identification and reporting changes limit local inference.
Ten people were killed in collisions involving e-scooters in 2025, all of whom were e-scooter riders, compared with 6 in 2024.
Small counts are volatile and nationally aggregated.
Zero source roles were promoted to exact-address evidence, parcel risk, candidate values or business rows.
